# /write-brief <contract-id>

## 1. Ask the runtime first

Run `pnpm pactwright context <contract-id>` for the current lineage and `pnpm pactwright lifecycle status --intent <intent-id>` for the completed stages. The runtime owns the lifecycle: it decides what is permitted, who may decide and how records are linked. Never reason about that yourself.
If the runtime reports a validation problem, or lists `write-brief` as already completed, show its output and stop. The runtime refuses any record that is out of order.

## 2. Write the brief

Use the `spec` agent (from `.claude/agents/spec.md`) for this. Give it the runtime context verbatim. Inspect the relevant project and repository state and write one focused brief for the contract. Reference the contract; do not copy it.

## 3. Hand the result to the runtime

Write a YAML file in a temporary location outside the repository with:

```yaml
contract: <contract-id>
title: <brief title>
body: |
  <brief>
```

Then run `pnpm pactwright lifecycle record write-brief --file <path>`.
The runtime checks the transition, validates the complete graph and writes
the record. Do not create or edit anything under `specs/` yourself.

## 4. Stop

Show the runtime output verbatim and stop. Do not run another adapter
command; the user decides what to do next.
